title: Secure BackOffice Browser Sessions
readerIntent: Configure and verify secure Axis employee login, restoration, locking, and logout.
priorKnowledge: Understand employee authentication and browser security basics.
owner: Profile owns browser-session security; Axis holds presentation and an in-memory access token
summary: Axis uses short-lived in-memory employee access tokens and an optional Profile-owned rotating refresh session in a scoped HttpOnly cookie, protected by exact origins and CSRF proof.

sections.heading: Session flow
items: Employee credentials are submitted only to Profile's browser-authenticate route.
Profile returns a short-lived employee access token for Axis memory and writes the refresh credential to a scoped HttpOnly cookie that JavaScript cannot read.
After browser refresh, Axis calls the restore route with credentials enabled and copies the readable CSRF cookie value into X-CSRF-Token.
Profile verifies the exact allowed Origin, atomically consumes the refresh state, rotates both credentials, and returns only the replacement access token and employee identifier.
Logout revokes refresh state, expires both cookies, and Axis immediately removes its in-memory access token.

sections.heading: Configuration
items: The Profile browser-session facade is disabled by default and must be enabled through layered profileBrowserSession configuration.
Configure an explicit allowlist of credentialed-CORS origins; a wildcard origin is invalid for credentialed sessions.
Align the CSRF cookie name with the Axis public runtime setting.
Require HTTPS and Secure cookies in production; non-Secure cookies are restricted to explicitly allowed loopback HTTP development origins.
Use a strict shared auth cache with atomic consume and local fallback disabled when more than one process or node can serve the session.

sections.heading: Locking is not logout
paragraphs: The Axis idle lock screen hides the workspace and requires the configured re-entry behavior, but it does not silently change Profile token, refresh, revocation, or expiry policy. Security-sensitive environments may configure logout instead of local locking.

sections.heading: Threat and verification checklist
items: Wrong password, customer account, inactive/locked employee, missing enterprise, wrong origin, missing/mismatched CSRF, expired cookie, refresh replay, concurrent restore, and revoked session fail safely.
Only one concurrent refresh succeeds; a replaced or stolen refresh value cannot be replayed.
Access and refresh credentials never enter localStorage, sessionStorage, URLs, logs, telemetry, CMS content, generated context, or error responses.
Test page refresh, multi-tab behavior, idle lock, logout, network interruption, Profile restart, shared-cache outage, cookie scope, accessibility, and regression.
